text:
A: Hiya. Can you hear me okay?
B: Yeah. You're Lorraine as well, aren't you. I saw the name.
A: I am, yes! I thought that was funny. Wrexham, near enough.
B: Wednesbury. Black Country.
A: Oh, not too far, then. Are you alright? You look a bit fed up, sorry.
B: No, I'm alright. It's just been a lot of talking. I'm not used to it.
A: No, me neither. I'm usually stood in my kitchen talking to the radio.
B: I liked your kitchen, in your picture. It's like mine. I've got the same bread bin, I think.
A: The cream one? From B&M?
B: Yeah.
A: There you go, then. Are you working, love?
B: No. I was a machinist, till the firm shut. Eighteen months now.
A: Oh, I'm the same, sort of. I took redundancy from the college last year. I'm looking at school kitchens and that now.
B: I applied for a school kitchen. Never heard nothing back.
A: They don't, do they. You fill in all them pages and then nothing. It knocks you a bit.
B: It does. I hate the forms. And the interview, sitting there with someone half your age asking where you see yourself in five years. I don't know. On me settee.
A: That's what I'd say! I'd never dare, mind.
B: I would. That's probably why they don't ring.
A: Have you got kids?
B: One. Kieran, fifteen. He's on his phone all hours, I don't know who he's talking to. It worries me sick, if I'm honest.
A: Oh, they're all like it. My son was the same at that age, and he's lovely now. Lives in Chester with his partner. You'd not believe it was the same lad.
B: Hope so. Do you go away at all? Holidays?
A: Caravan, mostly. Talacre, or Abersoch if we're feeling posh.
B: We do Prestatyn! That's next to Talacre, isn't it?
A: Right next door. We've probably been in the same chippy.
B: Probably. Gary likes the one on the front. I don't like flying, so.
A: No, I'm the same. I went to Majorca with my sister twice and I held her hand the whole way.
B: I don't talk to mine.
A: Oh. I'm sorry, love.
B: It's alright. Long story. ...Did you see Corrie last night?
A: I did, yes. I couldn't believe it when she —
